Occupational, Geriatric & Mental Health

Community care of special groups — workers, older adults and people with mental illness.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe occupational health care in the community
  • Describe care of the elderly
  • Describe community mental health care
  • List the nurse’s roles for these groups

In simple words

Some groups need special community care: workers exposed to hazards, older adults with age-related problems, and people with mental illness in the community. The nurse identifies, teaches, supports and links them to services.

Occupational health

  • Goal: protect workers from hazards and promote their health
  • Hazards: dust (silicosis), chemicals, noise, heat, radiation, ergonomic strain
  • Health check: pre-placement and periodic medical checks, PFT and audiometry
  • Safety: helmets, gloves, goggles, safe machinery, rest breaks
  • Programmes: ESI (Employees’ State Insurance) provides care and cash benefits

Geriatric health

Problem Care
Frailty and falls Home safety, grip rails, exercise, review medicines
Cataract and hearing or vision loss Screening, aids, spectacles
Diabetes, hypertension, heart disease Regular check-up, medicines, diet
Dementia Orientation, routine, safe home, family support
Depression and loneliness Activities, family contact, day care
Caregiver burden Training, respite care, counselling
Elder abuse Report and protect; include in care plans

Community mental health

  • Promote mental health and prevent relapse
  • Identify early signs of illness and suicide risk
  • Support adherence to medicines and support groups
  • Rehabilitation and social integration, reduce stigma
  • Support families and caregiver training
  • Refer to DMHP or specialised services when needed

🔴 Keep older people independent

The aim of geriatric care is ability, not dependence. Encourage activity, safe home, family contact and timely treatment. A fall is not normal ageing — assess it.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Occupational health checks pre-placement and periodically.
  2. PPE prevents occupational injuries and exposures.
  3. ESI provides medical care and cash benefit for workers.
  4. Falls in old age need assessment, not acceptance.
  5. DMHP delivers community mental health care.
  6. Reduce stigma; rehabilitate rather than institutionalise.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Silicosis is seen in workers exposed to silica dust.
  2. Pre-placement checks prevent unfit workers from hazardous jobs.
  3. Day care, respite and support groups prevent caregiver burnout.
  4. Confidentiality protects the job of a person with HIV or mental illness.
  5. Screen older adults for vision, hearing and cognitive change.

📌 Memory trick

Geriatric care: M-A-D-E — Medicines review, Activity, Diet, Eye and ear care.

60-second revision

  • Workers: hazard control, PPE, health checks, ESI.
  • Older adults: independence, falls, vision, dementia, caregiver support.
  • Community mental health: identify early, adherence, rehabilitation, reduce stigma.
  • Nurse’s role: identify, teach, support, link, report.

Test yourself

Pre-placement health checks in industry are meant to:

Answer: B. Pre-placement examination prevents a worker from being placed in a job that could damage his health.

Which protects a worker from chemical exposure?

Answer: B. Personal protective equipment such as gloves, goggles and aprons prevents exposure to hazardous chemicals.

A frequent fall in an older person should be:

Answer: B. Falls are never normal; check vision, balance, medicines and hazards in the home.

Community mental health is delivered through:

Answer: B. The District Mental Health Programme delivers mental health care in the community with trained teams.

Silicosis is seen in workers exposed to:

Answer: A. Silicosis is a fibrotic lung disease caused by long exposure to silica dust in mining, stone crushing and sand blasting.
